subject: paired t-test as a simple latent change score model

messages.author: cd3acd6a194a56a6
messages.subject: paired t-test as a simple latent change score model
parts:
I posted this on cross-validated a bit ago, but figured I would try here too...

I am trying to estimate the following path model: 




which is taken from (http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3794455/). 

As shown in the picture, the model has the following constraints: 

1. gamma is either estimated or fixed at zero (I am trying to fix to zero here).
2. No Y2 residual error; 
3. Intercept of Y2 is set to zero; 
4. The auto-regressive path is set to 1; 
5. The LCS to Y2 path is set to 1; 
6. Both Y1 and Y2 are "baseline" mean centered - centered on the mean of Y1 (Y2_bl_ctr and Y2_bl_ctr in the code below). 

I am trying to implement this as follows (See comments for how I am trying to implement each constraint)

    test <- '
      # measurement model
        lcs =~ 1*Y2_bl_ctr #4 - the LCS to Y2 path is set to 1
      # regressions
        lcs ~ 0*Y1_bl_ctr #gamma is set to 0 for equivilance with the t-test
        Y2_bl_ctr ~ 1*Y1_bl_ctr #3 - The auto-regressive path is set to 1
      # residual error
        lcs ~~ 1*lcs
        Y2_bl_ctr ~~ 0*Y2_bl_ctr #1 - No Y2 residual error
    '



summary(test <- lavaan(test
                       ,data=dat
                       ,int.lv.free = TRUE #intercepts of LCS is to be estimated
                       ,int.ov.free = FALSE #2- Intercept of Y2 is set to zero;
                       )
        )



But this is giving me the following warning messages: 

#** WARNING ** lavaan (0.5-20) model has NOT been fitted #** WARNING ** Estimates below are simply the starting values

Shouldn't setting
int.lv.free = TRUE
force the lavaan function to still estimate an intercept, even if I have fixed everything else in the model?

Well, that was embarrassing (latent variable newb here).

I needed to specify the intercept in the regression model as follows:
